title: Purity for a finite normal cover over a depth-two local base
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal local domain, with closed point $a\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ (normal means integral domain and integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]; local means it has a unique maximal ideal). Let $q:L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be quasi-compact, quasi-separated, smooth with geometrically connected fibres [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $V\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$ be the open whose points are exactly those different from $a$. Let $n:N\to L$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with every local ring of $N$ a normal domain. Assume the open $n^{-1}(q^{-1}(V))$ is dense in $N$ and $n|_{q^{-1}(V)}$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $W\subset L$ be open and $x\in W$ satisfy $q(x)=a$ and $n|_W$ etale. If $\operatorname{depth}A\ge2$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], then $n$ is etale.

proof.text: Let T be the union of q inverse V and W. Etaleness is local on the target, so the restriction of n to T is finite etale. Every fibre over a point different from a is entirely contained in T. The closed fibre is integral because q is smooth and geometrically connected, and W meets it, so T is dense on it.

For each base point of depth at most one the entire fibre is in T: the only possibly missing base point is a, whose depth is at least two. Apply Tag 0EYB to obtain a finite etale extension E over L. The depth calculation in that theorem is the flat local depth formula 0337; its construction and uniqueness are the depth-two extension 0EY6.

Smoothness over the normal base makes L normal; E is normal by etaleness. Density excludes vertical components of N. Both N and E have the same generic finite algebra, since they agree on q inverse V. A finite normal algebra is the full integral closure of the base in its generic algebra: an integral element over the base is integral over that algebra, hence lies in it by normality. Thus both algebras agree on every affine chart and the identifications glue over L. Transport etaleness across this isomorphism.
